title: Q3 2025 plan and financial update, with 2025 deficit
subtitle: Procurement review requested, falling development charge collections, low tax stabilization reserve, transit revenue shortfall, Cambridge budget night scheduling
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council receive the Q3 2025 Plan and Financial Update for information and amend the 2025 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix D {{vote:m1}}. Because this is a committee, Council still has to adopt the recommendation.

Staff projected an operating shortfall of about $3.8 million, or 0.7% of the regional property tax levy. Policy requires it to be covered from the Tax Stabilization Reserve. The main causes are lower transit fare revenue, lower Provincial Offences Act revenue and the cost of winter maintenance. Staff said the reserve will end the year well below the 3 to 5% of operating budget generally considered healthy, and that they are reviewing how to rebuild it. Regional development charge collections also fell sharply, which staff linked to the housing market and recent provincial legislation.

The committee also received the quarterly report on tenders and proposals approved by the CAO. It asked finance staff to report back on whether the Region should keep awarding some contracts on lowest price. Staff will look at Cambridge budget night scheduling, which overlaps with another community event.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council receive the Q3 update for information, which shows progress on the Annual Business Plan and the financial position.
The committee recommended amending the 2025 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix D, which staff described as minor adjustments to cash flow timing between projects.

debate: On procurement, one councillor asked how Regional rules support buying local during the trade war. Staff said trade agreements allow little local preference but that contract extensions, subcontracting and a competitive local supplier base help, and that most suppliers are based in Ontario.

Several councillors said they do not favour awarding contracts on lowest price alone, citing cost increases after award. The chair said the Region's pre-qualification of bidders reduces that risk, but agreed more discussion was warranted. Staff said reviewing the policy would mean reopening the procurement by-law, and offered to share the current by-law with members first.

On the reserve, a councillor noted the Tax Stabilization Reserve would fall to a historic low and urged caution. Staff said that policy lets only surpluses replenish it, and that finance will review whether that is enough.

On development charges, a councillor asked whether the Province knows of the shortfall and could help. Staff said other municipalities see similar declines, the cause is not yet clearly split between legislation and the economy, and they would support raising it once the data is clear.
On transit, the chair said inaccurate student population estimates from post-secondary institutions drove much of the ridership revenue shortfall, and called for better data to help the Region plan.
